title: Fpqc descent of multiplicative type
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $H\to S$ be an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Give $H$ the structure of an $S$-group scheme: multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams. Such a group is of multiplicative type if on an fppf covering of $S$ [def-pc-fppf-site] it is isomorphic to $D_U(M)=\operatorname{Spec}_U\mathcal O_U[M]$ for finitely generated abelian groups $M$, with Hopf operations as in [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]; the relative spectrum is obtained by gluing the affine group-algebra spectra. Let $\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. If each $H\times_SS_i$ is of multiplicative type, then $H$ is of multiplicative type. No Noetherian, reducedness, smoothness, connectedness or residue-characteristic hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(1), printed pp.299-300; this is descent for fpqc-local forms, not assertion (2) concerning extensions. WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf; online statement and proof read. No Stacks tag states this structural result.

proof.text: For an integer $n>1$ let $p_n:H\to H$ be the scheme morphism $h\mapsto h^n$ formed from the multiplication and diagonal, and put $P_n=H\times_{H,p_n,e}S$. This construction does not require $H$ to be commutative. The fibre-product universal property identifies $(P_n)_T$ with the identity fibre of the power map on $H_T$, for every $T\to S$: both represent pairs consisting of a point of $H_T$ and the equality of its $n$th power with the identity. On a split chart the Hopf formulas give $p_n^*(e_m)=e_{nm}$.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(1), printed pp.299-300, proof via Theorem B.4.1; explicit torsion-kernel descent argument following that criterion.

proof.text: For each $i$, take an fppf splitting cover $\{U_{ia}\to S_i\}$ with $H_{U_{ia}}\simeq D_{U_{ia}}(M_{ia})$. Character duality applied to $n:M_{ia}\to M_{ia}$ identifies $(P_n)_{U_{ia}}$ with $D_{U_{ia}}(M_{ia}/nM_{ia})$. If $m_1,\ldots,m_d$ generate $M_{ia}$, reducing their coefficients modulo $n$ gives a surjection $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}^d\twoheadrightarrow M_{ia}/nM_{ia}$, so this quotient is finite. On every nonempty affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset U_{ia}$, the algebra $A[M_{ia}/nM_{ia}]$ has the finite basis $\{e_{\bar m}\}$. The finite-free-algebra spectrum lemma therefore makes $(P_n)_{U_{ia}}\to U_{ia}$ finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. These properties hold on all such affine opens, as required by their local definitions. Empty opens impose no condition.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(1), printed pp.299-300, proof via Theorem B.4.1; explicit torsion-kernel descent argument following that criterion.

proof.text: An fppf covering is fpqc. Apply fpqc descent of finiteness, flatness and local finite presentation separately to $P_n\times_SS_i\to S_i$ along its splitting cover $\{U_{ia}\to S_i\}$. This proves all three properties over every $S_i$. Apply the same three descent statements again along the given fpqc family $\{S_i\to S\}$. Consequently $P_n\to S$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, for every $n>1$. Both applications concern actual base changes of the same scheme morphism by step 1; neither application assumes the cover is a singleton or that its members are Noetherian.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(1), printed pp.299-300, proof via Theorem B.4.1; explicit torsion-kernel descent argument following that criterion.

proof.text: Apply the finite-flat rank statement to $P_n\to S$. It says that $s\mapsto\dim_{\kappa(s)}\Gamma((P_n)_s,\mathcal O_{(P_n)_s})$ is locally constant. Step 1 identifies $(P_n)_s$ with $H_s[n]$, so these are exactly the functions $d_n$ required in the fibral criterion. Finiteness in step 3 also gives finiteness of each fibre, by the same rank statement's finite-dimensional fibre description.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(1), printed pp.299-300, proof via Theorem B.4.1; explicit torsion-kernel descent argument following that criterion.

proof.text: For every $s\in S$, choose $i$ and $t\in S_i$ mapping to $s$, using joint surjectivity of the fpqc covering. Choose a splitting member $U_{ia}$ and $u\in U_{ia}$ mapping to $t$, using joint surjectivity of the fppf covering. The residue maps give $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(t)\to\kappa(u)$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(u)$. Restricting the splitting along $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U_{ia}$ gives $H_\Omega\simeq D_\Omega(M_{ia})$: on affine charts the base-change identification is the explicit isomorphism $A[M_{ia}]\otimes_A\Omega\simeq\Omega[M_{ia}]$, $e_m\otimes c\mapsto c e_m$, respecting each Hopf operation. Thus condition (a) of the criterion holds with the algebraically closed extension $\Omega/\kappa(s)$. No rational point over an algebraic closure of $\kappa(s)$, and no descent of an isomorphism along a field extension, is being assumed.

source.place: Corollary B.4.2(1), printed pp.299-300, proof via Theorem B.4.1; explicit torsion-kernel descent argument following that criterion.

proof.text: The affine, flat and finite-presentation hypotheses on $H\to S$ are the hypotheses of the item. Step 5 verifies the geometric-fibre condition of the fibral criterion, and steps 3-4 verify its finite torsion fibres and local constancy condition for every integer $n>1$. Apply that criterion with $G=H$. It supplies an fppf covering on which $H$ is diagonalizable with finitely generated character groups, precisely the asserted multiplicative-type conclusion. This also covers the empty base, when all the pointwise conditions are vacuous.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q105-b1bc041d9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Conrad's Reductive group schemes online; it is not under literature/. The item is Cor B.4.2(1) (pp.299-300): an fppf affine group that is fpqc-locally of multiplicative type is of multiplicative type. The new node lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-fibral-criterion is the sufficiency half of Thm B.4.1 (p.297). Its hypotheses: G affine, flat and finitely presented; for each point, G becomes diagonalizable over some algebraically closed extension, which need not be algebraic (allowed by the opening of B.4); each torsion fibre G_s[n] is finite and its order d_n is locally constant. Neither the node nor the source assumes G is commutative, and G_s[n] is taken as the scheme fibre of the power map. Small cases checked: mu_p in char p, constant Z/p over Z_p (fails the fibre condition), and Conrad's DVR example (fibres fine, orders jump, so it fails). The node does not duplicate B.3.2, B.4.2(2) or the field-only definition node, and it does not restate the item. Steps 1-6 check out. (1) Fibre-product pasting identifies P_n with each fibre's n-torsion, and p_n^*e_m=e_{nm}. (2) Character duality with u=n gives D(M/nM) on nonempty affine opens, finite free by Stacks 02KB. (3) An fppf cover is fpqc (Stacks 022C); descent of finite, flat and lfp (02LA, 02L2, 02KY) is applied first along the splitting cover, then along {S_i->S}. (4) The rank node (04MH) makes d_n locally constant. (5) Joint surjectivity plus an algebraic closure of kappa(u) gives the geometric splitting. (6) The criterion applies. The item statement is unchanged and not weakened. Batch-5 check: lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc is the general topology fact Stacks 022C, not part of the trace formula or Poincare duality or their proofs. Character duality reaches the trace-formula chapter only through that same lemma. Both citations accepted. Accepted tool_uses: finite-free spectrum and the three fpqc descents. No fixes.
